name: node
one_liner: The core JavaScript runtime that powers most of the internet's backend servers — free, foundational infrastructure, not a product.
buyer: No direct buyer — this is pure infrastructure used for free by virtually every web company on earth.
business_use_cases: Every backend web development shop builds client server applications on top of it as their runtime.
A hosting company offers managed Node.js hosting and deployment as their paid product, with Node itself as the free foundation.
A training company teaches Node.js fundamentals as part of paid bootcamp curriculum.

money_ideas.idea: No direct monetization of Node itself; the real money is in hosting, consulting, or training services built around it

steal_this: Not this specific repo — it's plumbing; any opportunity is in services built on top (hosting, consulting, training), not in Node.js itself.
